input.topic: Vitamin B3 Deficiency: Dementia Is A Complication

expected.question_text: A 47-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of diarrhea. He has a history of hepatitis C, intravenous substance use disorder, and alcohol use disorder. The diarrhea has been persistent for the past 3 months; it is nonbloody and is not associated with vomiting. On examination, the patient has sunken eyes, a dry tongue, and a hyperpigmented, pruritic rash over his arms, legs, and face. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 104/min, respirations are 19/min, and blood pressure is 105/85 mm Hg. A deficiency of some kind is suspected. Left untreated, this patient will most likely develop which of the following?
expected.explanation_footer:
Vitamin B 3 (Niacin) | Function | - Essential nutrient involved in the synthesis and metabolism of carbohydrates, fatty acids, and proteins | |---|---| | Deficiency | - Pellagra - Diarrhea - Photosensitive pigmented dermatitis - Dementia | | Sources | - Plant and animal foods | This patient has vitamin B 3 (niacin) deficiency . The initial manifestation of niacin deficiency is diarrhea, followed by pruritic dermatitis in sun-exposed areas. If niacin deficiency remains uncorrected, it will eventually progress to dementia . Niacin is important as a cofactor in oxidation-reduction biochemical reactions that involve NAD and NADP. It is also essential in the synthesis and metabolism of carbohydrates, fatty acids, and proteins. Niacin deficiency causes pellagra , which consists of diarrhea, pigmented dermatitis, and, eventually, dementia. Given that this patient has a history of alcohol use disorder and intravenous substance use disorder, it is likely that he has poor nutrition leading to the deficiency of key nutrients. https://d2vrujxrqm3l5p.cloudfront.net/ab3876b8-7c58-4a92-a43a-2192b96f0dea.png The swollen, roughened, and mottled pigmentation of the skin is the classic dermatologic finding in pellagra secondary to niacin deficiency.

Pellagra (diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia) is a manifestation of vitamin B 3 (niacin) deficiency.
